review_notes: retain_terminal_damage assigns a new composition revision; only accepted matching native completion calls presented(receipt_revision), so failed/deferred/dropped/capture attempts retain the lease. Older presentation cannot retire a newer lease.

Before a new prepared composition, old lease transfers back to producer and merges with newer pending damage; it does not overwrite producer state. A successful older native frame only retires its derived lease, not subsequent producer output.
Partial multi-pane snapshot failure restores all previously consumed panes. take_render_state creates its fallible snapshot before taking pending damage, so the failing pane itself keeps damage.

Preparation failure restores lease immediately; later encoding/acquisition/presentation failure leaves it owned for reuse or next rebuild. Closed dock restores producer damage before creating empty lease, preserving hidden state.

Metadata vector, cloned session strings and damage vectors are allocated in render-terminal-damage-lease scope; allocation owner follows buffers returned for merge. Scope accounting is observation of owned bytes, not itself full host/process budget qualification.
No new terminal authority, parser/input semantics or private mutation path introduced. Existing RenderSession recovery transfer carries lease; clear_content does not erase it.

Verified retained-board precondition occurs before take_active_tab_render_states, so an absent retained scene cannot consume new terminal damage without establishing a lease. Any prior lease has already been restored to producer before this precondition failure.
